title: Global Metro Purchasing Power Comparison Report 2026
subtitle: Bilateral head-to-head empirical purchasing power modeling across premier international relocation corridors.
metaDescription: Compare net purchasing power, rent burdens, and disposable income differences across NYC, London, Dubai, Toronto, Sydney, and Singapore.
citationString: LivWorthy Research Institute. (2026). Global Metro Purchasing Power Comparison Report. https://www.livworthy.com/reports/purchasing-power-comparison
methodologyNotes: Models true net after-tax salary retention against localized basket of housing, transport, groceries, and utilities.
Housing comparisons reflect median 1-bedroom city center benchmarks from national statistical agencies.
FX valuations reflect dated benchmark baseline snapshots (1 USD = 0.79 GBP, 3.67 AED, 1.36 CAD, 1.52 AUD, 0.92 EUR).

primarySources.name: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS CEX)

summaryInsights: Relocating from London to Dubai on equivalent senior packages yields an average 38% increase in discretionary savings due to 0% PIT and competitive utility structures.
A New York salary of $100,000 matches the lifestyle purchasing power of approximately £68,500 in London or 285,000 AED in Dubai.
Munich requires approximately €8,500 more gross salary than Berlin to maintain identical housing and uncommitted savings buffers.
tableRows: Higher NYC gross offset by lower London nominal rent
Dubai 0% PIT produces +42% higher annual cash retention
Elimination of UK 40% higher-rate tax expands savings by £18,000+
Vancouver rent carries a 6% premium over Toronto central core (+6%)
Melbourne housing offers 20% savings compared to Sydney inner-ring (-20%)
Identical federal tax schedules, but Munich rent is 28% higher than Berlin
Both boast low/zero personal income tax; Dubai rents offer larger unit footprints
